identity.title: ALMA resolves the hourglass magnetic field in G31.41+0.31

question.value: What is the magnetic field morphology and strength in the hot molecular core G31.41+0.31 at ~0.2'' resolution, and does the field prevent fragmentation and collapse?

evidence.quote: To better establish the role that the magnetic field plays in the collapse of G31.41+0.31, we carried out Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the polarized dust continuum emission at 1.3 mm
as part of project 2015.1.00072.S (P.I.: M. Beltrán)
The observations were performed in Band 6 centered at 233 GHz and with the array in the C40–5 configuration.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four 2 GHz spectral windows of 64 channels each (TDM, 31.25 MHz per channel), full polarization

evidence.quote: a spectral setup with four 2 GHz spectral windows of 64 channels each (TDM mode with 31.25 MHz resolution per channel)
the array in the C40–5 configuration
The baselines of the observations range from $\sim$17 to 2647 m.
The resulting synthesized CLEANed beam of the maps is $0.28\ensuremath{''}\times0.20\ensuremath{''}$ at a position angle PA of $-60^\circ$.
The rms noise of the maps is 1.2 mJy beam$^{-1}$ for Stokes $I$ and 22 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ for Stokes $Q$ and $U$.
carried out with ALMA in Cycle 4 on July 12, 2017
as part of project 2015.1.00072.S (P.I.: M. Beltrán)

analysis_steps.goal: Image Stokes I, Q, U and derive polarization quantities

method.value: CLEAN imaging with natural weighting; P=sqrt(Q^2+U^2), p=P/I, psi=0.5 arctan(U/Q); segments rotated 90 deg for B field

evidence.quote: we derived the linear polarization intensity, $P=\sqrt{Q^2+U^2}$, the fractional linear polarization, $p=P/I$, and the polarization position angle

assumptions.value: Polarization from magnetically aligned dust grains

evidence.quote: Assuming that the polarization is produced by magnetically aligned dust grains

validation.value: Self-calibration tested but not helpful; scattering ruled out by comparison with SMA 870 um pattern and polarization fractions

evidence.quote: We performed self-calibration using the total intensity (Stokes $I$) image as a model but the images did not improve and we decided not to apply it.

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate line contamination of Stokes I flux

method.value: Scale 217 GHz continuum flux of BEL18 to 233 GHz with S~nu^(2+beta), beta=1 and 2, compare with measured flux

evidence.quote: We used two different values of the dust emissivity index, $\beta=1$ and 2, and estimated a dust continuum emission flux of 4.64 and 4.98 Jy, respectively.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit magnetostatic toroid model to polarization angles

method.value: DustPol models for grid of lambda (1.63, 2.66, 8.38), b0, phi, i; synthetic maps via simobserve/simanalyze; chi-squared on polarization angles within 5 sigma contour

evidence.quote: For each combination of $\lambda$, $b_0$, $\varphi$, and $i$, we performed a chi-squared test for the difference between the observed and the modeled polarization angles within the $5\sigma$ contour
we set the effective sound speed to 1.4 km s$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: Isothermal model, axially symmetric singular toroid; temperature profile from BEL18

evidence.quote: The model is isothermal, and the value of the sound speed provides the scaling for both the density and the magnetic field strength.

fitting.value: Reduced chi-squared grid; 1 sigma errors from the method of Lampton et al. 1976

evidence.quote: The $1\sigma$ errors have been estimated using the method of Lampton et al. ((cite: lampton76)).

validation.value: lambda=8.38 discarded because G31 is optically thick; constant temperature 250 K tested; b0>0.1 discarded

evidence.quote: This allowed us to discard the case $\lambda=8.38$, since we know that G31 is optically thick toward the center (BEL18).

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate B strength with DCF method

method.value: B_pos = xi*sigma_los/dpsi_int*sqrt(4 pi rho); dispersion from Gaussian fits to residual histogram (4 deg bins) in 15 sigma region; B=B_pos/cos i

evidence.quote: Our modeling provides the inclination with respect to the plane of the sky, $i$, which allows us to estimate the total magnetic field strength as $B=B_{\rm pos}/\cos i \simeq8$–13 mG

key_parameters.value: sigma_los=2.1 km/s from DeltaV~5 km/s; n=1.4e7 cm-3; R=1.1''; sigma_psi=27.6 and 17.3 deg

evidence.quote: Using $\Delta V\simeq5$ km s$^{-1}$, the value of $\sigma_{\rm los}$ is 2.1 km s$^{-1}$.
Assuming a distance of 3.7 kpc, the mass of the Main core is $\sim$26 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$

findings_qualitative.value: Hourglass-shaped field is confirmed down to <1000 au scales and is perpendicular to the NE-SW velocity gradient, supporting rotation over the outflow interpretation

evidence.quote: it supports the hypothesis that the velocity gradient is due to rotation and discards the molecular outflow scenario proposed by Araya et al.

findings_qualitative.value: Field deviates from model near embedded sources, NE core and outflow walls

evidence.quote: our model fails to properly describe the magnetic field close to the center of the Main core, around the NE core, and at the northern and southwestern edges of the Main core

claims.hypothesis: The field in G31 is an hourglass consistent with a magnetized toroid
claims.experiment: Fit DustPol toroid models to ALMA 1.3 mm polarization angles
claims.result: Best model lambda=2.66, i=-45 deg, phi=-44 deg, b0<=0.1
claims.finding: Field is nearly poloidal and hourglass-shaped down to <1000 au

evidence.quote: The polarized emission in the Main core of G31.41+0.41is successfully fit with a semi-analytical magnetostatic model of a toroid supported by magnetic fields.

claims.hypothesis: The NE-SW velocity gradient is due to rotation
claims.experiment: Compare field axis orientation with velocity gradient
claims.finding: Gradient is rotation, with little effect on the field

evidence.quote: This supports the hypothesis that the velocity gradient is due to rotation of the core and suggests that such a rotation has little effect on the magnetic field.

claims.experiment: DCF field strength and mass-to-flux ratio
claims.finding: Slightly supercritical; field does not prevent fragmentation and collapse

evidence.quote: implies that the mass-to-flux ratio in this region is slightly supercritical ($\lambda$=1.4–2.2)

why_this_data.value: Four times higher resolution than previous SMA data, comparable to separation of embedded centimeter sources

evidence.quote: which is four times higher than that of previous (sub)millimeter observations (GIR09) and is similar to the separation of the centimeter continuum sources

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Dust self-scattering rejected as origin of polarization since pattern matches 870 um SMA and fractions reach 4-5%

evidence.quote: This suggests that the polarization observations are likely tracing the emission of magnetically-aligned grains and are not affected by dust scattering

limitations_admitted.value: Stokes I flux is an upper limit because of line contamination; polarization fractions are lower limits

evidence.quote: the polarization fraction has to be taken as a lower limit

limitations_admitted.value: Mass-to-flux ratio is a lower limit because the core mass and stellar content may be underestimated

evidence.quote: the observed value of the mass-to-flux ratio should be taken as a lower limit

referee_caveats_inferred: Model lacks turbulent component, so residual dispersion is large and DCF dispersions are bracketed by two Gaussian-fit choices
Only three lambda values were sampled, and distance changed from 7.9 to 3.7 kpc, which affects mass and flux
Single-star mass assumption and spherical geometry affect lambda
TDM spectral resolution contaminates Stokes I, affecting polarization fractions
